WHAT WAS CHANGED\
\
**Read path, line 13:** `data/raw/eDNA_yell_2023` becomes `data/raw`. The 02 notebook downloads the reads straight into `data/raw/`, so the manifest was pointing at files that don’t exist, and `qiime tools import` failed.

**Metadata row:** I’m adding `Site1f_S92` → `Site1`. It’s in the manifest but was missing from `sample-metadata.tsv`, which would make later QIIME steps that use the metadata fail.

# Create manifest so QIIME knows where the reads are

```{bash}

cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

raw=$(realpath ../../data/raw)

# manifest: sample name, R1 path, R2 path
printf "sample-id\tforward-absolute-filepath\treverse-absolute-filepath\n" > manifest.tsv


for sample in Site1J_S99 Site1L_S101 Site1U_S114 Site1a_S83 Site1aa_S130 Site1b_S84 Site1bb_S139 Site1c_S85 Site1cc_S140 Site1d_S86 Site1dd_S141 Site1e_S91 Site1ee_S142 Site1f_S92 Site1g_S93 Site1h_S94 Site1k_S100 Site1m_S102 Site1n_S103 Site1o_S104 Site1p_S105 Site1q_S106 Site1r_S111 Site1s_S112 Site1t_S113 Site1v_S117 Site1w_S118 Site1x_S119 Site1y_S120 Site1z_S129 Site5J_S107 Site5L_S109 Site5a_S87 Site5aa_S132 Site5b_S88 Site5bb_S133 Site5c_S89 Site5cc_S134 Site5d_S90 Site5dd_S135 Site5e_S95 Site5ee_S136 Site5f_S96 Site5ff_S137 Site5g_S97 Site5gg_S138 Site5h_S98 Site5k_S108 Site5m_S110 Site5n_S115 Site5o_S116 Site5p_S121 Site5q_S122 Site5r_S123 Site5s_S124 Site5u_S126 Site5v_S127 Site5w_S128 Site5z_S131; do
```

# Import reads onto QIIM 2

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime tools import \
  --type 'SampleData[PairedEndSequencesWithQuality]' \
  --input-path manifest.tsv \
  --input-format PairedEndFastqManifestPhred33V2 \
  --output-path demux.qza
```


# Check read quality

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime demux summarize \
  --i-data demux.qza \
  --o-visualization demux.qzv
```


# Remove primers

--p-front-f: the primer at the start of R1. ^ means “at the very start of the read”
--p-front-r: the primer at the start of R2
The part after ... is the other primer, flipped (reverse complement). The V9 region is short, so a read often runs past the end of it into the other primer. When that happens, cutadapt cuts off that primer and everything after it. ;optional means the read is kept even if this second primer isn’t there
--p-discard-untrimmed: throw away reads without the V9 primers
--p-nextseq-trim 20: trim low-quality bases from the read ends (a fix for the NextSeq sequencer)
--p-minimum-length 50: drop reads shorter than 50 bases after trimming


```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime cutadapt trim-paired \
  --i-demultiplexed-sequences demux.qza \
  --p-front-f "^GTACACACCGCCCGTC...GTAGGTGAACCTGCAGAAGGATCA;optional" \
  --p-front-r "^TGATCCTTCTGCAGGTTCACCTAC...GACGGGCGGTGTGTAC;optional" \
  --p-discard-untrimmed \
  --p-nextseq-trim 20 \
  --p-minimum-length 50 \
  --p-cores 8 \
  --o-trimmed-sequences V9-demux.qza \
  --o-stats V9-cutadapt-stats.qza
```




Clean up the reads with DADA2

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime dada2 denoise-paired \
  --i-demultiplexed-seqs V9-demux.qza \
  --p-trunc-len-f 0 \
  --p-trunc-len-r 0 \
  --p-n-threads 16 \
  --o-table V9-table.qza \
  --o-representative-sequences V9-rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-denoising-stats V9-dada2-stats.qza \
  --o-base-transition-stats V9-dada2-error-model.qza
```


Turn the DADA2 stats into a report you can view. It shows how many reads were kept at each step (input → filtered → denoised → merged → non-chimeric).

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime metadata tabulate \
  --m-input-file V9-dada2-stats.qza \
  --o-visualization V9-dada2-stats.qzv
```
